apps.summary: Life360 lets family members see each other's locations and get driving and crash alerts. To do that, it collects precise location, movement and driving data. According to its privacy policy (26 Aug 2026), it may also share that data with business partners for their own commercial use, and offer aggregated driving data to help insurers model driving behaviour. One partner, Arity (owned by Allstate), is the subject of ongoing lawsuits over how driving data from apps like Life360 was used; nothing is proven, and Life360 isn't a defendant. If you want the family features without the partner sharing, Life360's own settings let you turn most of it off.

consequences.text: The Texas AG and a federal class action allege that Allstate's Arity paid apps such as Life360 to embed its SDK. Both say Arity built a driving database on 45 million+ Americans and sold the data to insurers, who used it to raise premiums. Life360 is not a defendant.
consequences.wording: Alleged by the Texas AG and in a federal class action; not proven in court. Part of the Texas case was dismissed on jurisdiction grounds and is under appeal.

procedural_note.text: On 2025-04-10 the Texas court dismissed The Allstate Corporation and Arity 875 LLC for lack of personal jurisdiction (MLex); that dismissal is on appeal and the case continues against the remaining Allstate entities.
